Interactive NFL EPA Scatter

Saiem Gilani

Source: vignettes/recipe-nfl-epa-interactive.Rmd
recipe-nfl-epa-interactive.Rmd
On this page

The brief: the team’s website wants the season’s offense-vs-defense chart as something readers can explore: point at any logo and see the team’s EPA per play on both sides of the ball and where that ranks. It is the interactive version of the NFL EPA Scatter recipe, with the same data and the same flipped defense axis. ggiraph’s girafe() turns the ggplot into an interactive SVG, and geom_sdv_logos_interactive() gives each logo a hover target.

library(sdvplotR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(ggiraph)

season <- 2025

1. Get the data

The same table as the static recipe: one season of play-by-play, cut to regular-season runs and passes with an EPA value, averaged by the team with the ball and by the team on defense, then ranked. A tooltip should name the team, so the full name comes from sdv_teams(), joined on the team id that sdv_resolve() finds for each nflverse abbreviation.

plays <- nflreadr::load_pbp(season) |>
  filter(season_type == "REG", play_type %in% c("pass", "run"), !is.na(epa))

offense <- plays |>
  group_by(team = posteam) |>
  summarise(off_epa = mean(epa), plays = n())
defense <- plays |>
  group_by(team = defteam) |>
  summarise(def_epa = mean(epa))
stopifnot(is.character(offense$team), is.character(defense$team)) # one type on both sides of the key

team_names <- sdv_teams("nfl") |> select(team_id, name)
teams <- inner_join(offense, defense, by = "team") |>
  mutate(
    off_rank = min_rank(desc(off_epa)),
    def_rank = min_rank(def_epa), # less EPA allowed is better
    team_id = sdv_resolve(team, league = "nfl")
  ) |>
  inner_join(team_names, by = "team_id")
stopifnot(nrow(teams) == 32)
head(teams)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   team  off_epa plays  def_epa off_rank def_rank team_id name             
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <int>    <dbl>    <int>    <int> <chr>   <chr>            
#> 1 ARI   -0.0185  1074  0.0884        23       27 22      Arizona Cardinals
#> 2 ATL   -0.0214  1036 -0.00374       24       15 1       Atlanta Falcons  
#> 3 BAL    0.0340   956  0.0251        12       21 33      Baltimore Ravens 
#> 4 BUF    0.136   1065 -0.0163         3       13 2       Buffalo Bills    
#> 5 CAR   -0.0393   996  0.0673        26       23 29      Carolina Panthers
#> 6 CHI    0.0795  1096  0.0181         8       19 3       Chicago Bears

The page embeds this table, not the play-by-play: 32 rows, one per logo.

2. Logos with hover details

geom_sdv_logos_interactive() is geom_sdv_logos() plus an invisible point over each logo that takes the hover. tooltip and data_id go in the same aes() as team. The tooltip is HTML, so <br> breaks the lines and <b> sets the name in bold. The quadrant layers are the static recipe’s: the league-average lines, a label in each corner, and scale_y_reverse() so the best defenses are on top.

corners <- data.frame(
  x = c(Inf, -Inf, Inf, -Inf),
  y = c(-Inf, -Inf, Inf, Inf), # reversed scale: -Inf is the top
  label = c(
    "Good offense, good defense", "Bad offense, good defense",
    "Good offense, bad defense", "Bad offense, bad defense"
  ),
  hjust = c(1.02, -0.02, 1.02, -0.02),
  vjust = c(1.5, 1.5, -0.6, -0.6)
)

quadrants <- list(
  geom_mean_lines(aes(x0 = off_epa, y0 = def_epa), color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4),
  geom_text(
    aes(x, y, label = label, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust),
    data = corners, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3, color = "grey55", fontface = "italic"
  ),
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.07)),
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = 0.12))
)

teams <- teams |>
  mutate(tip = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b><br>Offense: %+.3f EPA per play (No. %d)<br>Defense: %+.3f EPA per play allowed (No. %d)",
    name, off_epa, off_rank, def_epa, def_rank
  ))

The chart is the static recipe’s with one layer swapped: geom_sdv_logos_interactive() in place of geom_sdv_logos(). data_id names each hover target; the next step uses it to tell the hovered team from the other 31. hover_size makes each target about as wide as its logo.

p_epa <- ggplot(teams, aes(off_epa, def_epa)) +
  quadrants +
  geom_sdv_logos_interactive(
    aes(team = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = team),
    league = "nfl", width = 0.055, hover_size = 14
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste("NFL offense vs defense,", season, "regular season"),
    subtitle = "EPA per play on runs and passes. Defense axis flipped: up and right is better.",
    x = "Offense EPA per play", y = "Defense EPA per play allowed",
    caption = "Data: nflverse via nflreadr  |  Chart: sdvplotR"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey45", size = 7.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

3. Hover one team to fade the rest

girafe() draws the ggplot as an interactive SVG, and its options style the hover. opts_tooltip() gives the tooltip a white card. ggiraph styles the element under the pointer with opts_hover() and every other element with a data_id with opts_hover_inv(). A logo is an image, which that CSS cannot fade, so the fade is done by the hover targets: opts_hover_inv() paints the other 31 targets white at 75% opacity, a veil over each logo, and opts_hover() keeps the hovered team’s target clear.

epa_widget <- girafe(
  ggobj = p_epa, width_svg = 7, height_svg = 4.4,
  options = list(
    opts_tooltip(css = "background:white;color:#222;padding:6px 8px;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);font-size:12px;"),
    opts_hover(css = "fill:none;stroke:none;"),
    opts_hover_inv(css = "fill:white;fill-opacity:0.75;stroke:none;"),
    opts_toolbar(saveaspng = FALSE)
  )
)
epa_widget

Point at a logo in the middle of the pack, where the static chart’s logos overlap: the tooltip names the team and the other logos fade, so no logo has to be found by eye. The veil sits on top of the logos because the hover targets are the layer drawn after them; a team half under a neighbor keeps a faint edge of the neighbor’s veil.

The SVG embeds a copy of each logo, at most 160 px a side (the max_px argument), so the 32 logos add about half a megabyte to the page. For a page of several charts, the cookbook’s headshot-in-tooltip recipe loads images by link instead.

4. Share it

htmlwidgets::saveWidget() writes the chart to one HTML file. selfcontained = TRUE inlines ggiraph’s JavaScript, and the 32 logos already travel inside the SVG, so the file opens anywhere with no folder beside it and no network (it needs pandoc, which ships with RStudio).

out <- tempfile("sdvplotR-recipe-")
dir.create(out)
html <- file.path(out, "nfl_epa_interactive.html")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(epa_widget, html, selfcontained = TRUE, title = "NFL offense vs defense")
round(file.size(html) / 1024) # kilobytes
#> [1] 9046

5. The static version

girafe() draws a ggplot, so the same object prints as a static chart, for a post or a slide: the interactive layers draw as their plain counterparts. ggsave() exports it as in the static recipe.

p_epa
